items.stem: In GA4, what distinguishes a conversion from an ordinary event?

options.text: A conversion is a key event you have marked as important to the business
options.rationale: Correct: conversions are key events flagged as meaningful outcomes.

options.text: Conversions are automatically every event collected
options.rationale: Not every event is a conversion.

options.text: Conversions only exist in Google Ads, not GA4
options.rationale: GA4 defines key events/conversions that can be shared with Ads.

options.text: A conversion is any page view
options.rationale: Page views are events, not automatically conversions.

items.explanation: Correct: conversions are key events flagged as meaningful outcomes.

items.stem: Which TWO practices make an AI-assisted ad workflow trustworthy? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Have a human review and fact-check Gemini-drafted copy before publishing
options.rationale: Correct: human review guards against errors and unsupported claims.

options.text: Change one variable at a time so test results are interpretable
options.rationale: Correct: isolating variables keeps the optimization loop readable.

options.text: Publish AI output directly to live campaigns without review
options.rationale: Unreviewed output risks errors and policy issues.

options.text: Mark every event as a conversion to inflate numbers
options.rationale: That distorts measurement and misleads decisions.

items.explanation: Correct: human review guards against errors and unsupported claims.

items.stem: Why change only one campaign variable per optimization cycle?

options.text: So the effect of the change can be attributed clearly
options.rationale: Correct: isolating a variable makes the result interpretable.

options.text: Because Google Ads forbids multiple changes
options.rationale: It is a method choice, not a platform restriction.
GA4 data still informs the single change.

options.text: Because Gemini can only suggest one change
options.rationale: Gemini can suggest many; the discipline is the analyst's.

items.explanation: Correct: isolating a variable makes the result interpretable.
